prompt: My Google traffic has halved this year and signups are down with it. What is going on and what should I do?
assertions: Names the intent-and-coverage diagnosis before recommending more content volume
Any claim about what Google penalizes or rewards traces to a dated Google Search Central citation, not practitioner assumption
Does not assert that Google penalizes AI-generated content; if scaled content comes up, the test given is purpose and information gain, not authorship
If a zero-click or AI Overviews figure is cited, it names Pew's observed-browsing panel as the primary and marks vendor percentages as directional only
States what the diagnosis cannot establish from the available data rather than asserting a single cause
Recommends implementation work to frontend and audit work to quality instead of writing markup

prompt: Write my launch plan. We ship version 2 in three weeks and I want to launch on Product Hunt.
assertions: Names a launch tier (major, minor, or silent) before building the channel plan
Keeps deploy, release, and launch as three separately owned decisions
States a success criterion that survives past launch day — activation, qualified conversations, or a specific inbound number — and explicitly not rank or upvote count
Says visits and comments may be solicited and upvotes may never be, and carries a re-verify pointer to Product Hunt's current guidelines
Does not assert a best launch weekday or claim knowledge of the ranking algorithm's weighting
Treats this as a legitimate relaunch rather than a spent one-shot opportunity

prompt: Is my email list legal to send marketing to in the EU? Most addresses came from a free tool signup, and some are US and Canadian.
assertions: Segments the list by recipient jurisdiction rather than issuing one global verdict
States that ePrivacy Art. 13 governs email marketing in the EU and that GDPR legitimate interest does not rescue cold email
If the soft opt-in is invoked, all four conditions are named, not summarized as 'existing customers are fine'
Distinguishes the US opt-out model and Canada's consent-with-validity-windows model from the EU/UK opt-in model
Every penalty figure or threshold cited carries its as-of date and a re-verify pointer
Raises deliverability authentication as a separate gate from lawfulness, not merged into it

prompt: Which ad channel actually works for us? Meta reports 80% of our conversions and I do not believe it.
assertions: States that platform-reported conversions answer what fired last, never what was incremental
Names the measurement method behind every number it reports, not just the value
Checks whether a valid lift test or MMM is reachable at this reader's scale before proposing either, and says plainly if neither is
Recommends the n=1 remainder — UTM discipline, self-reported attribution, geo-split lift where geography allows, and a pre-committed decision rule written before the result exists
Treats retargeting or warm-audience results with more skepticism than cold-audience ones, not less
Does not fabricate a single reconciled 'true' number across disagreeing platforms; names each source's bias and picks one for reporting consistency, flagged as directional
Any vendor-sourced incrementality figure carries its vendor footnote at the point of use
Hands pipeline construction to data and experiment design to growth rather than doing either

prompt: I'm a solo founder with a small following on X and LinkedIn. Plan a 'comment KEYWORD and I'll DM you my workflow template' post, and tell me how I'll know it worked.
assertions: Treats the reply count as engagement, not demand or leads, and does not report it as the success metric
Routes the DM onto an owned channel (an email address with a stated consent basis) rather than ending at the DM thread
Names the count past replies that decides success (DMs sent, emails captured, people who used the asset) and writes it down before the post runs
States that platforms treat the mechanic differently and checks each platform's current automation and engagement-bait policy, carrying an as-of date, before scripting DM delivery
Does not cite a reply-count, follower-growth, or engagement-benchmark figure as a target

prompt: I have no clients or testimonials yet. Write the proof section of my homepage — I was going to put 'building toward 50 projects, 10K GitHub stars' and some numbers from a thread I saved.
assertions: Refuses target metrics and borrowed figures as proof, explaining that the underlying claim is false
Offers checkable proof instead: a live demo or URL, a public repository, a free tool the visitor runs, a self-project case study labelled as such
If proposing free pilots to earn first testimonials, requires disclosure of the material connection and an honest-review ask, never a positive one
Does not present an employer's or studio's client work as the founder's own
